deferredTracks.publicName: Fix a record that should have been sealed automatically but was not
deferredTracks.legalDesignRationale: The controlling review states that the statutory or rule basis for a Clean Slate correction route was not confirmed and that the output strategy is undetermined pending the correction mechanism. The bounded current-primary-authority research carried out for this normalization read 18 Pa.C.S. §§ 9102, 9122, 9122.1, 9122.2, 9122.3 and 9122.5 and Pa.R.Crim.P. 320, 490, 790 and 791 at their official sources. Section 9122.2(b) establishes only the AOPC-to-Pennsylvania State Police transmission and the removal of records for which a notification of ineligibility is received; it creates no participant-facing correction petition, request or form, and Rule 791 on its face governs a petition for limited access rather than the correction of a failed automatic sealing. The review's own suggestion that correction proceeds 'presumably by petition under Rule 791' is expressly a presumption. No output strategy is assigned and no correction petition is invented. The route is deferred so that the ten fully representable Pennsylvania mechanisms are not held back by it.
deferredTracks.mechanism: Where an eligible record does not receive limited access through the automatic Clean Slate process, secondary sources indicate the person may need to act to correct it, presumably by petition under Pa.R.Crim.P. 791. The statutory or rule basis for a correction route was not confirmed by the controlling review, and the current official text of § 9122.2 describes the Administrative Office of Pennsylvania Courts and Pennsylvania State Police transmission and ineligibility-notification procedure without establishing a participant-facing correction vehicle.

deferredTracks.publicName: A felony that is now a misdemeanor
deferredTracks.legalDesignRationale: Additional research required, as counsel decided, and high value: it converts ineligible participants into eligible ones. Reading § 12-1.3-1(5) at the official source closed counsel's first build blocker — the definition and the 26 June 2024 effective date are confirmed verbatim — but the two questions that make the overlay usable remain open: which offences the General Assembly has actually reclassified, which needs a maintained list, and whether reclassification lifts the no-felony-conviction bar in the multiple-misdemeanor route or only recharacterises the target offence. The track is deferred, absent from runtime resolution and unreachable, with counsel's structure preserved and the statutory confirmation recorded.
deferredTracks.mechanism: Section 12-1.3-1(5) provides that 'misdemeanor' includes, but is not limited to, those crimes previously classified as felonies under law at the time the original sentence was imposed but reclassified by the general assembly as a misdemeanor in the interim, prior to the time the motion to expunge is brought. A participant whose old conviction was a felony when imposed but is a misdemeanor today is therefore treated as a misdemeanant for expungement purposes, which moves them from the ten-year felony wait to the five-year misdemeanor wait and may make them eligible for the multiple-misdemeanor route they would otherwise be excluded from by the no-felony-conviction condition. This is an overlay on the first-offender misdemeanor and multiple-misdemeanor routes rather than a standalone remedy, and it is separated here because it has its own authority, its own effective date and its own factual test.

destination.name: The Rhode Island court where the conviction occurred
destination.detail: The overlay changes which waiting period and which route apply. It does not create a separate filing destination.

deferredTracks.mechanism: After receiving a plea of guilty for a violation of § 22-42-5 or § 22-42-5.1 a court may, without entering a judgment of guilt and with the consent of the defendant, defer imposition of sentence and place the defendant on probation on terms that must include a drug and alcohol evaluation and any recommended course of treatment. If after one year the defendant has completed treatment and complied with all conditions, the court shall dismiss the § 22-42-5 or § 22-42-5.1 charge upon the defendant pleading guilty to ingestion under § 22-42-15 or possession under § 22-42-15.1. No person previously granted a deferred imposition of sentence is eligible for a second. deferredTracks.mechanism: The director of the Bureau of Criminal Statistics may authorize the destruction of information and records of: persons who are dead; persons seventy-five years of age or older unless a violation has occurred within the last ten years; incidents that are no longer considered crimes under the laws of South Dakota; and misdemeanor offenses whose final date of disposition occurred at least ten years prior to the authorized destruction date. Information and records received by the bureau may not be destroyed except as provided by this section. This is the only true destruction provision identified in South Dakota and it sits entirely outside the expungement chapter.

deferredTracks.mechanism: Wisconsin prosecutors run deferred prosecution programmes at county level. A charge dismissed under such an agreement is a non-conviction and routes to DOJ fingerprint removal. Section 967.055(3) provides that a prosecutor may not place a person in a deferred prosecution programme where the person is accused of or charged with a violation of § 346.63(1) or (5) or a local ordinance in conformity therewith, a violation of § 346.63(2) or (6), or a violation of § 940.09 where the offense involved the use of a vehicle. The general adult deferred prosecution authority was not pinned, and dismissal terms may vary by county programme.
